## Goal

Deliver a minimal reference builder that turns a game's source into a loadable runtime artifact (ESM entry + assets + manifest entry), defining the contract every `tce-<game>` repo will follow.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). No Vite library-mode game build exists today; without it the loader's end-to-end AC cannot be demonstrated with a real game. Scope is deliberately minimal: one script + docs, not a full per-game release pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/build-game-artifact.mjs` builds one game (via `--game <id>` / the selected preset entry) in Vite library mode into `build/game-artifacts/<id>/`, emitting an ESM `entry.js`.
- The build externalises `phaser` and the `@core-engine/*`, `@card-system/*`, `@rule-engine/*`, `@ui/*`, `@ai/*` aliases so the artifact does not bundle a second Phaser/engine copy (verified by asserting those specifiers are absent from the emitted bundle and importing them at runtime from the launcher).
- The emitted artifact re-exports the game's scene class and `GAME_INFO` in a shape the loader consumes, and copies its declared thumbnail asset into `assets/`.
- The script can emit or merge a `manifest.json` entry (id, sceneKey, title, description, thumbnail, coreEngineVersion, entry) for the built game.
- A test builds a fixture game (or golf) and asserts the artifact loads through `loadGamePlugins` with a stubbed importer.
- The build output directory is gitignored and does not dirty the working tree.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `scripts/build-game-artifact.mjs` (Vite `build.lib`, `rollupOptions.external`).
- Add an npm script `build:game-artifact`.
- Add `tests/scripts/build-game-artifact.test.ts` (or a focused smoke script).
- Update `.gitignore` for `build/game-artifacts/`.

## Key Files

- `scripts/build-game-artifact.mjs`
- `package.json`
- `.gitignore`
- `tests/scripts/build-game-artifact.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- F4 dynamic ESM import & scene registration.
data.title: Reference game artifact builder

## Goal

Verify the complete runtime plugin flow end-to-end in the packaged Electron launcher — the acceptance gate for the parent feature's AC1–AC4.

## Context

Part of FEATURE: Electron runtime game plugin loader (CG-0MTRO7VMI000F3A5). This is the dedicated verification slice; it consumes the builder (F7) and the boot wiring (F6). Because the Electron runtime is not covered by the standard browser suite, this item records a repeatable runbook plus scripted checks where feasible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Full project test suite must pass** with the loader present (no regression for build-time presets).
- With a real artifact dropped into `<contentDir>/games/` plus a valid `manifest.json`, launching `npm run start:electron` shows the game in the Game Selector alongside static games, and it is playable.
- With an incompatible `coreEngineVersion`, the game is hidden and the incompatibility notice names the game and required range.
- With `games/manifest.json` missing or malformed, the launcher boots and lists only the static games; an error is logged.
- The same three scenarios are exercised by an automated check (browser/unit harness with the loader + a stub host where a full Electron launch is impractical), and the packaged runbook documents the manual steps and expected observations.
- Evidence (commands, observed output/notes) is recorded on the work item; the verification is repeatable using only committed scripts/docs.

- **Full project test suite passes** with the loader present (no regression for build-time presets): the unit/browser suites run green at the verification commit.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a runbook under `docs/dev/` or the work-item comment describing the three packaged scenarios.
- Add an automated scenario test exercising the loader with the F7 artifact and the F1 fixtures.
- Record results as a work-item comment.

## Key Files

- `tests/ui/game-plugin-e2e.test.ts`
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- `scripts/build-game-artifact.mjs`

## Dependencies

- F6 Electron boot wiring & graceful degradation.
- F7 reference game artifact builder.

## Goal

## Context

## Acceptance Criteria

- **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **All related documentation updated** — `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the `games/manifest.json` schema (field-by-field), the artifact layout (`games/<id>/entry.js`, `assets/…`), the `coreEngineVersion` compatibility rule, and the `tce-games://` asset protocol.

data.description:
## Goal

Fix the shared `HandView` so that, when `maxSlots` is set, card and outline positions derive from the hand's **capacity** rather than the current card count — adding a card never moves an existing card or slot.

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. Sibling test items add the failing unit and browser tests first.

Root cause: `computeCardPositions()` builds a row centred on `this.cards.length` (`layoutCardPositions({ count: this.cards.length, … })`), and `_computeOutlineSlots()` ghosts it (plus appending extras). The empty-hand branch already lays out the desired fixed `maxSlots` row, so that row is the template to reuse. `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path all re-derive the row/rotation normalisation from the occupied positions and must move to the template as well. `setMaxSlots()` currently only rebuilds outlines and does not re-lay the cards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1–AC5: implement the capacity-template behaviour — outline slot positions identical for a hand of 0…`maxSlots` cards; `addCard` fills the next slot right of the occupied run while pre-existing card positions are unchanged; occupied outlines still match card `x/y/rotation` with extras below every card; `setMaxSlots(n)` is the only mutation that re-lays the row and always yields exactly `n` slots; the empty-hand capacity row is unchanged (same centred straight/arc row the cards will occupy).
- Add a shared private helper in `src/ui/HandView.ts` that derives the `maxSlots` template with the existing `layoutCardPositions` maths (gap = `spacing - cardWidth`, `centerX`, `maxWidth` compression, `arcRadius` Y) and the template-span rotation normalisation; recompute from current options on each use (no stale cache).
- `computeCardPositions()` horizontal returns the first `cards.length` template positions; over-capacity cards continue with the template step to the right (best-effort, no re-centring).
- `getInsertionPosition(index)` returns the template position at `index` (first `maxSlots`; template step beyond), so Market→hand transfer animations land exactly on the resting card.
- `_computeOutlineSlots()` derives all `count` slots from the same template (occupied slots ghost the card's **actual** sprite rotation, extras keep `depth = index - 0.5 - count`), replacing the per-count ghosting/extension branch.
- Rotation and arc normalisation in `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, and the animated `sortCards` path use the template span when `maxSlots` is set, so per-card rotation is also stable across adds.
- `setMaxSlots(maxSlots)` re-lays the cards (calls `applyLayout()`), not just the outlines.
- Capacity-driven layout is keyed on `maxSlots !== undefined`, independent of `showPositionOutlines`; toggling outlines never moves cards.
- Hands without `maxSlots` keep the existing centred-on-count layout; vertical cascade keeps `baseY + i * spacing` and is not regressed.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` is reused unchanged.
- The sibling unit and browser test items pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/ui/handView.outlines.test.ts`).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — `computeCardPositions()`, `_computeOutlineSlots()`, `getInsertionPosition()`, `rebuildDisplay()`, `applyLayout()`, `sortCards()` animated path, `setMaxSlots()`.
- `src/ui/layoutCardPositions.ts` — reused to build the capacity row (no change expected).

**Deliverables:**

- Capacity-driven `HandView` layout with stable card and outline slots and green sibling tests.
data.title: Capacity-driven HandView slot template

## Goal

Document the capacity-driven (stable) slot semantics and remove stale wording that describes the hand as centred on the **current** card count (parent AC8).

## Context

Parent: CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ. The fix changes documented behaviour, so the doc-update policy applies: the change and its docs must ship together (or this child blocks parent closure).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC8: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (Hand capacity outlines), `AGENTS.md` if the documented behaviour changes, and any relevant Gym/docs entries.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Hand capacity outlines" states that when `maxSlots` is set the slot row is derived from **capacity**, cards fill it left-to-right, occupied card/slot positions do not move as cards are added, and `setMaxSlots()` is the only operation that re-lays the row; the empty-hand row is unchanged.
- `AGENTS.md` §2 (HandView/PileView key features) hand bullet updated to say slots/outlines are capacity-derived and stable across adds.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` help text describes the fixed-slot behaviour instead of implying per-count centring.
- Stale per-count-centring comments corrected in at least: `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` ("centred on handCenterX" / "left-anchored slot estimate"), `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` ("centred on handCenterX"), and `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTutorialHints.ts` (hand-zone comment).
- No player- or developer-facing text still claims the hand is centred on the current card count when `maxSlots` is set.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — "Hand capacity outlines" section.
- `./AGENTS.md` — §2 hand bullet (and §9 if it repeats the layout claim).
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — help text.

## Summary

The F1-approved follow-detection mechanism — `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(developerSteamID)` — is **not exposed** by `steamworks.js`, the only maintained npm binding for the Steamworks SDK (verified: v0.4.0 exposes achievement/apps/auth/cloud/input/localplayer/matchmaking/networking/overlay/stats/utils/workshop namespaces, but **no `friends` namespace**).

As a result, the launcher shipped on CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC implements:
- real SDK store-page opening via `overlay.activateToStore` / `activateToWebPage`,
- real Steamworks init (`init` + `restartAppIfNecessary` + app id bootstrap),
- follow detection **capability-detected**: `followCheckSupported = false` when the binding lacks the API, with a persisted **manual self-attest claim** fallback.

This delivers the feature with graceful degradation, but does **not** achieve fully automatic follow detection.

## Desired outcome

Automatic follow detection that survives an audit of intake AC2 ("the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks"), via one of:

- (a) A small **custom native addon** wrapping `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` (N-API), shipped alongside `steamworks.js`; the existing `SteamworksClientLike.friends.isFollowing` seam means no TypeScript change is needed once present.
- (b) A newer `steamworks.js` release (or a fork) that exposes `friends.isFollowing`.
- (c) A publisher-backend Steam Web API check (needs a server component; previously scoped out).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A concrete mechanism exposing `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` is available to the Electron main process.
- [ ] `SteamworksFollowSource.followCheckSupported` becomes `true` on a real Steam session and automatic unlock is verified end-to-end with a real Steam account.
- [ ] No regression to the graceful-degradation path (absent module → unavailable, no crash).
- [ ] Automated tests cover the new detection path with a fake module.

## Relationship

Discovered while implementing CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC (F3). Follow-up, not a blocker: the shipped feature degrades to a manual claim.
data.title: Steam follow detection: expose ISteamFriends::IsFollowing via a native addon or newer binding

## Goal

Have Golf, Coloretto and Lost Cities report their terminal win outcome through the engine-generic contract, with no Steam SDK code in any game module.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of `../tce-golf`, `../tce-coloretto`, `../tce-lost-cities` calls the engine game-outcome surface on a completed win, using the same `gameId` as the launcher catalog/manifest.
- No Steamworks or Electron import appears in any game repo.
- In the browser/headless build the call is a no-op (no-op sink) and gameplay is unaffected.
- Each game repo's unit tests cover win-to-outcome reporting.
- The change is committed and pushed to each repo's `dev` branch (never `main`) and recorded on this item; tests pass under `--project unit` in each affected repo.

## Key Files

- `../tce-golf/src/scenes/GolfScene.ts`
- `../tce-coloretto/src/scenes/ColorettoScene.ts`
- `../tce-lost-cities/src/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts`
- `../tce-golf/src/GolfAchievements.ts` (new per-repo reporting helper)

## Deliverables

Cross-repo outcome wiring + tests on `dev`, with results recorded here.
data.title: Wire Golf, Coloretto and Lost Cities to report win outcomes

## Goal

A main-process service that evaluates the give-away config against locally-unlocked achievements and persists game unlocks through the shared store, reachable from the renderer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GiveawayService` reads `SteamAchievementService.getUnlocked()`, evaluates the F1 contract against the give-away config, and persists unlocks to the unified `ContentUnlockStore`; it runs on launch and after each achievement unlock and never throws.
- `SteamFollowService` and `GiveawayService` share one unlock store so the Game Selector has a single source of truth; existing follow unlock behaviour is preserved and its existing tests still pass.
- IPC channels plus `electron/preload.cjs` expose give-away status/progress and a refresh call; channel names stay in sync and every handler is total.
- With Steam, the manifest, or the config absent the service degrades to a safe no-op (no fabricated unlock, no crash) and the web build is unaffected.
- Unit tests (mocked sources/stores) cover launch evaluation, post-unlock evaluation, idempotence, cross-launch persistence, and missing-dependency degradation; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`
- `electron/steam-achievements-ipc.ts`
- `electron/steam-follow-ipc.ts`
- `electron/preload.cjs`
- `electron/main.ts`
- `tests/steam-giveaways/giveaway-service.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Give-away service, unified store wiring, IPC/preload surface, unit tests.
data.title: Give-away service with unified unlock persistence and IPC

## Goal

Show locked give-away games in the Game Selector with the milestones still required, and unlock them live when the triggers are met.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unified lock computation consumes follow + give-away status and returns, per gated game, a lock reason and progress (remaining milestone titles/count); existing follow lock behaviour is preserved.
- `GameSelectorScene` renders SLL-compliant locked cards with progress (e.g. "1 of 2 milestones") and updates when a give-away unlocks; overlay/label objects follow the documented depth/parenting conventions.
- In a plain browser (no bridge) no game is locked and the app is fully playable.
- Unit tests cover mixed states (follow-unlocked, achievement-partial, achievement-complete, base content) and a browser test covers the rendered locked/progress state.
- Tests pass under `--project unit` and `--project browser`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/steam-lock.ts`
- `src/ui/steam-giveaways-client.ts` (new)
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts`
- `tests/ui/steam-lock.test.ts`
- `tests/ui/GameSelectorGiveaways.browser.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Unified lock model, renderer client, selector UI, unit + browser tests.

## Goal

Record the producer's decision — three give-aways (Golf, Coloretto, Lost Cities) triggered by "win your first game" plus "win in a second distinct game" — as versioned, game-agnostic config with drift detection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.json` lists exactly the three games (`golf`, `coloretto`, `lost-cities`) with their required achievement ids, plus a `_comment` recording the rationale and the no-overlap-with-the-follow-bonus (Feudalism) rule.
- The bonus catalog is extended so all four gated games (Feudalism follow bonus plus the three give-aways) resolve in the launcher, with no hard-coded titles in logic.
- A validator detects config drift — unknown game id, unknown achievement id, and overlap with the follow bonus — and an automated test fails on each case.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `README.md` document the config format, how to add/retarget a give-away, and the business-decision process.
- Unit tests for the validator pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.json` (new)
- `electron/bonus-catalog.json`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- `README.md`
- `tests/steam-giveaways/giveaway-config.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Give-away config, extended bonus catalog, drift validator + tests, docs.
data.title: Give-away config, catalog extension and drift validator

## Goal

## Acceptance Criteria
